pr_title: Change DH_get_nid() to set the value of q if it is not already set
pr_body:
Fixes #11108.

It only sets q if a valid named group is found.
The function signature was recently changed to pass a non const DH pointer
in order to allow the nid to be cached internally. As an extension of this
the value of q can now also be set as q is always known for named groups.
If q is set then the length is also set for this case.

reason. I think there is the code assumes that if q is set that
it's a safe prime. We should probably document something related

I Temporarily added a prime test of q for all the modp and ffdhe groups that we have to verify this..

In the case that q was manually set - it checks that it equals (p - 1) / 2 - Which is documented..

got them right... So it doesnt look like they are. Is that your question??

Are you happy for me to change them to 2 * value in the tables in Sp800-56ar3?

Also SP800-56Ar3 does say that the modp group are safe primes.. (Thought I read it somewhere quite a while ago).

I'm not sure what nbit is supposed to contain, but it's assigned to
length. I assume DH_get_length() returns this. According to the
manpage, that means:
The length parameter indicates the length of the secret exponent (private key) in bit

I didn't know that it returned that.

So you now seem to assume that if q is set that length is also set. It might be want we want to do internally, but a user can set p and q, and not the length.

This is also a change in behavior if they only set p. By default we used to generate a private key that has 1 bit less then p, now we generate one that's twice as long as the security strength if we know p.
My previous comment is about the length not being set if q is set of course not the case, since the set0_pqg function did set it. But a user could override it and set it to 0 ...

> My previous comment is about the length not being set if q is set of course not the case, since the set0_pqg function did set it. But a user could override it and set it to 0 ...

Its all a bit tricky isnt it.. I guess I then need to be a bit more careful about where I set it.. And cater for if maybe being zero in some places.

So you want DH_set0_pqg() to say something like?

This method checks if the parameters associated with p and g and optionally q are associated with known safe prime groups. If it is a safe prime group then the value of q will be set to q = (p - 1 ) / 2 if q is NULL. For safe prime groups the optional length parameter is set to twice the value of the maximum_target_security_strength(BN_num_bits(p)) as listed in SP800-56Ar3 Table(s) 25 & 26.
If it is not a safe prime group then the optional length parameter will be set if q is not NULL to 
BN_num_bits(q).

issue_context.title: DH_generate_key requires q now
comments:
This seems to be new code introduced in commit f11f86f6ec7fb31bde1da2810ac975c032205321

@slontis: Can you look at it?

Thank you for finding this..

Note that you could also use DH_new_by_nid() instead of DH_new() for this case and you would not have seen the issue.

My testing suggests that f11f86f introduced an additional regression that is not fixed by #11114.
The scenario I am testing is (I'd provide sample code but I'm testing with Apache Tomcat and the Tomcat Native Connector so the test environment is non-trivial. I'm hoping my description will suffice.):

- server configured with RSA key/cert (no DH parameters present)
- server configured for TLSv1.2 only
- client attempting to connect with TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384

With 1.1.1 and master prior to f11f86f the client handshake succeeds. In master, after f11f86f the handshake fails. Applying #11114 does not resolve the issue.
If I call `SSL_CTX_set_dh_auto(c->ctx ,1);` at the end of the server SSL Context configuration, the client handshake succeeds again.

The issue appears to be `dh->length ==0` at [line 248 of dh_key.c](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/crypto/dh/dh_key.c#L248)
@markt-asf it is a similiar problem to the setting of q.. will include the fix in the same PR.

review_comments: This is not new behavior, but the code in 1.1.1 actually ignored the length if q was set, and uses BN_priv_rand_range(q). But from reading the manpage, this wasn't the behavior I expected, I expected it to remain 0. I'm also not sure why it's not using BN_priv_rand_range(p-1). So I think we should either not set dh->length in this case, or update the manpage.
Then I think we should correct the manpage.
